title: Quietly Soothing Greek Rice Pilaf
description: A comforting and gentle Greek dish perfect for a sick day, featuring tender rice and a hint of grassy freshness, this lacto-vegetarian friendly pilaf is made with baking powder and a special fry-grind-rice technique.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the rice to the saucepan and cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently, until the rice is lightly toasted.
Add the baking powder, dried parsley, salt, and black pepper to the saucepan and stir to combine.
Add the vegetable broth to the saucepan and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan with a tight-fitting lid, and simmer for 18 minutes, or until the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender.
Fluff the pilaf with a fork and stir in the crumbly feta cheese.
Serve the pilaf hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired.
